subject: Hospitality
title: How Airlines Invented Yield Management
description: One-minute skill: How Airlines Invented Yield Management.

hook.text: Two passengers on the same flight pay wildly different prices. This isn't a mistake—it's yield management, born in 1978.

buildup.text: After U.S. airline deregulation, carriers could set their own prices. American Airlines hired math PhDs to optimize fares.

discovery.text: The key insight: an empty seat on a departing flight is lost revenue forever. Perishable inventory must be priced dynamically.

twist.text: American Airlines' yield management system generated $1.4 billion in extra revenue over three years. Math beat intuition.

climax.text: Hotels saw the results and adopted the same approach. A hotel room is just like an airline seat—empty tonight means lost forever.

punchline.text: Empty seats, lost revenue. Airlines taught hotels to price by demand.

quiz.question: Why is a hotel room like an airline seat for pricing purposes?
options: Both are perishable—unsold tonight means revenue lost forever
